---
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
For each $n < \omega$,
\[
\mathsf{ZFC} \vdash \text{``}\{\alpha \in \operatorname{Ord} \mid V_{\alpha} \prec_{\Sigma_n} \mathbf{V}\} \text{ is a club''}.
\]
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\textit{For each} $n<\omega$ \textit{the following statement is provable
within} $\mathsf{ZFC}$:\smallskip

\begin{center}
$(\kappa $ \textit{is} $(n+1)$-\textit{Mahlo}) $\rightarrow $ $\exists
\alpha <\kappa $ $(\alpha $ is $n$-Mahlo and $V_{\alpha }\prec V_{\kappa
}).\medskip $
\end{center}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
Over $\mathsf{ZFC}$, the following schemes are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Lambda$;
\item for each $n<\omega$, arbitrarily large $n$-Mahlo cardinals $\kappa$
 satisfy $V_\kappa\prec_{\Sigma_n}V$;
\item for each $m,n<\omega$, arbitrarily large $m$-Mahlo cardinals $\kappa$
 satisfy $V_\kappa\prec_{\Sigma_n}V$;
\item for each definable club class $C$ of ordinals (with set parameters)
 and each $n<\omega$, $C$ contains an $n$-Mahlo cardinal.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
$\mathsf{ZFC}+\Lambda^{-}$ and $\mathsf{ZFC}+\Lambda$ are mutually interpretable.\footnote{However, the two theories are not bi-interpretable. This follows from a more general result asserting that any two bi-interpretable extensions of $\mathsf{ZF}$ (in the same language as $\mathsf{ZF}$) have the same deductive closure. See \cite{E-Visser,E-Visser-Corr}.}
Assuming the consistency of $\mathsf{ZFC}+$ ``there is an $\omega$-Mahlo cardinal'',
$\mathsf{ZFC}+\Lambda^{-}$ does not prove $\Lambda$.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
If $\mathcal M\models\mathsf{ZFC}+\Lambda$, then for every
$c\in M$, $L(c)^{\mathcal M}\models\Lambda$.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
Suppose $\mathcal M\models \mathsf{ZFC}+\Lambda$, $\mathbb P\in M$, and $G$
 is $\mathbb P$-generic over $\mathcal M$. Then $\mathcal M[G]\models\Lambda$.
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
Suppose $\mathsf{ZFC}+\Lambda$ is consistent. If $\psi$ is a sentence in the language of set theory satisfying either

\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathsf{ZFC}\vdash$ ``$\psi$ holds in $L$''; or

\item $\mathsf{ZFC}\vdash$ ``for some poset $\mathbb P$, $1_{\mathbb P}\Vdash\psi$''.
\end{enumerate}

Then there is a model of $\mathsf{ZFC}+\Lambda+\psi$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\textnormal{(MacDowell--Specker \cite{MacDowell-Specker}, Gaifman
\cite{G}, Phillips \cite{Phillips}).}
Every model $\mathcal M$ of $\mathsf{ZFC}^{-\infty}$ has a proper
elementary end extension $\mathcal N$.  Moreover, $\mathcal N$ can be
required to be both minimal and conservative over $\mathcal M$.
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
Suppose $\mathcal M$ is a model of $\mathsf{ZF}$ whose ordinal order has
cofinality $\aleph_0$, and let $\langle X,\lhd\rangle$ be a linear order
of arbitrary cardinality.  There is an elementary end extension
$\mathcal N$ of $\mathcal M$ whose ordinal order contains an isomorphic
copy of $\langle X,\lhd\rangle$ as indiscernibles above the ordinals of
$\mathcal M$.
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\textnormal{(\cite[Theorem C]{E-Deadends}).}
Every consistent extension $T$ of $\mathsf{ZF}$ has a model $\mathcal M$
of cardinality $\aleph_1$ such that $\mathcal M$ has no proper end
extension to a model of $\mathsf{ZF}$.
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
\textnormal{(\cite[Section 2]{E-5}).}
Let $T$ be a consistent completion of $\mathsf{ZFC}$. The following are
equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $T\vdash\Lambda$.
\item[(b)] There is a consistent theory $\overline T$ in a countable
expansion $\mathcal L$ of the language of set theory, containing a global
well-order, such that
\[
T+\mathsf{ZFC}(\mathcal L)\subseteq\overline T,
\]
and every model of $\overline T$ has a proper \emph{conservative elementary
end extension}.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- theorem-11: body_md -->
Suppose $T$ is a completion of $\mathsf{ZF}^{-\infty}$. For every uncountable cardinal $\theta$, $T$ has a $\theta$-like model.
<!-- end theorem-11 -->
<!-- theorem-12: body_md -->
\textnormal{(\cite[Theorem A]{E-4}).}
Suppose $\theta$ is an uncountable cardinal with the tree property, and
$T$ is a consistent completion of $\mathsf{ZFC}$. The following are
equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $T$ has a $\theta$-like model.
\item[(b)] $T$ contains the Levy scheme $\Lambda$.
\item[(c)] $T$ has a $\kappa$-like model for every uncountable cardinal
$\kappa$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-12 -->
<!-- theorem-13: body_md -->
\textnormal{(\cite[Theorem B]{E-4}).}
The following assertions are equiconsistent over $\mathsf{ZFC}$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] There is an $\omega$-Mahlo cardinal.
\item[(b)] For every finite language $\mathcal L$ expanding the language
of set theory, every $\aleph_2$-like model of
$\mathsf{ZFC}(\mathcal L)$ satisfies the corresponding expanded-language
scheme $\Lambda(\mathcal L)$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-13 -->
<!-- theorem-14: body_md -->
\label{thm:finite-automorphism}
Every consistent completion of $\mathsf{ZF}^{-\infty}$ has a model $\mathcal N$ that possesses a nontrivial
automorphism whose fixed point set is a proper initial segment of $\mathcal N$.
<!-- end theorem-14 -->
<!-- theorem-15: body_md -->
\textnormal{(\cite[Theorem A]{E-5}).}
Suppose $T$ is a consistent completion of $\mathsf{ZFC}+\Lambda$. There is a model $\mathcal M$
of $T+\mathsf{ZFC}(\vartriangleleft)+\mathsf{GW}$ such that $\mathcal M$
has a proper elementary end extension $\mathcal N$
possessing an automorphism whose fixed point set is precisely $M$.
<!-- end theorem-15 -->
<!-- theorem-16: body_md -->
\textnormal{(\cite[Theorem B]{E-5}).}
Let $\mathcal N=(N,\in,\vartriangleleft)$ satisfy
$\mathsf{EST}(\{\in,\vartriangleleft\})+\mathsf{GW}^*$, and let $j$ be an
automorphism of $\mathcal N$ whose fixed-point set $M$
is a proper $\vartriangleleft$-initial segment of $N$.
There is a family $\mathcal A$ of classes over the induced
structure $\mathcal M=(M,\in)$ such that
\[
 (\mathcal M,\mathcal A)\models
 \mathsf{GBC}+\text{``$\mathrm{Ord}$ is weakly compact''}.
\]
Consequently, $\mathcal M\models \mathsf{ZFC}+\Lambda$.
<!-- end theorem-16 -->
<!-- theorem-17: body_md -->
\textnormal{(\cite[Theorem 2.1]{E-5}).}
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] If $(\mathcal M,\mathcal A)\models
$ $\mathsf{GBC}+$ ``$\mathrm{Ord}$ is weakly compact'', then
$\mathcal M\models\mathsf{ZFC}+\Lambda$.
\item[(b)] Every consistent completion $T$ of $\mathsf{ZFC}+\Lambda$ has a
countable model $\mathcal M$ admitting an expansion
$(\mathcal M,\mathcal A)\models\mathsf{GBC}+$ ``$\mathrm{Ord}$ is weakly compact''.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-17 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\textnormal{(\cite[Corollary 2.1.1]{E-5}; see also
\cite[Theorem 2.4.12]{E-ZFI}).}
For every sentence $\varphi$ of the pure language of set theory,
\[
\mathsf{GBC}+\text{``$\mathrm{Ord}$ is weakly compact''}\vdash\varphi
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathsf{ZFC}+\Lambda\vdash\varphi.
\]
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\textnormal{(\cite[Definition 3.1]{E-ZFI}).}
The theory $\mathsf{ZFCI}_{<}$ is formulated in $\{\in,<,I\}$. In addition to
$\mathsf{ZFC}$ in this expanded language, it asserts that $<$ is a global
well-order satisfying the global-well-order axioms $\mathsf{GW}$, that $I$ is
cofinal in $\mathrm{Ord}$, and that $I$ is a class of order
indiscernibles for $(V,\in,<)$. Thus, for
each formula $\varphi(x_1,\ldots,x_k)$ in the language $\{\in,<\}$, and
any two increasing $k$-tuples from $I$, the truth value of $\varphi$
is the same on the two tuples.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- theorem-18: body_md -->
For every sentence $\varphi$ of the pure language of set theory,
the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathsf{ZFCI}^{-\infty}_{<}\vdash\varphi$;
\item $\mathsf{ZFC}^{-\infty}\vdash\varphi$;
\item $\mathsf{GBC}^{-\infty}+$ ``$\mathrm{Ord}$ is weakly compact'' $\vdash\varphi$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-18 -->
<!-- theorem-19: body_md -->
\textnormal{(\cite[Theorem 4.3]{E-ZFI}).}
For every sentence $\varphi$ of the pure language of set theory,
the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathsf{ZFCI}_{<}\vdash\varphi$;
\item $\mathsf{ZFC}+\Lambda\vdash\varphi$;
\item $\mathsf{GBC}+$ ``$\mathrm{Ord}$ is weakly compact'' $\vdash\varphi$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-19 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
For every consistent completion $T$ of $\mathsf{ZFC}$, the following are
equivalent: 

\begin{enumerate}
    \item $T\vdash\Lambda$.
   \item Some model of $T$ admits
an expansion to a model of $\mathsf{ZFCI}_{<}$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- theorem-20: body_md -->
\textnormal{(Solovay).}
$\mathsf{NFUA}$ and $\mathsf{ZFC}+\Lambda^{-}$ are equiconsistent.\footnote{Solovay's proof was never published, but it was circulated among the illuminati. The proof uses a combinatorial theorem of Schmerl \cite{Sch-1} concerning Mahlo cardinals of finite order, and is very different from the proof of Theorem \ref{My_thm_NFUA}.}
<!-- end theorem-20 -->
<!-- theorem-21: body_md -->
\label{My_thm_NFUA}
\textnormal{(\cite{E-5}).}
For a theory $T$ in the language $\{\in\}$, the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $T$ is a consistent completion of $\mathsf{ZFC}+\Lambda$.
\item There is a model $\mathcal A\models \mathsf{NFUA}$ such that
$T=\operatorname{Th}(CZ^{\mathcal A})$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-21 -->
